title: Stars and constellations
examples: Teacher, how do we know which stars belong together?
Can you show me a picture of the Plough in the sky?
Do all stars shine the same way?

explain.say: Look up at the night sky. Stars seem to make shapes.

items: We can see them every night.

explain.say: One famous star pattern is called the Plough.
The Plough is part of a bigger star pattern called the Great Bear.
Stars make their own light. They are huge balls of very hot gas.
The Sun is a star too. It is the star closest to us.
Long ago, sailors used the stars to find their way at night.

faq.a: A constellation is a group of stars that people see as a pattern or picture.

faq.q: Does the Plough move across the sky?
faq.a: Yes, the patterns of stars appear to move over the course of the night.
asks: Does the sky change at night?

faq.a: Stars shine because they are giant balls of hot gas that make their own light.
Yes. The Sun is a star. It is the closest star to Earth.
asks: Is the Sun like a star?

faq.a: The visible patterns can look different depending on where you are on Earth.
asks: Do all people see the same stars?

facts: Constellations are patterns made by groups of stars.
The Plough is a well-known pattern in the night sky.
Stars shine because they produce their own light.
The Sun is the star at the centre of our solar system.

quiz.say: Which one is a pattern of stars?
quiz.why: The Plough is a pattern made by seven bright stars.

wrong.0: The Moon is one big rock that goes around the Earth.
wrong.2: The Sun is one star on its own.

quiz.why: Stars are huge balls of very hot gas. They make their own light.

wrong.1: The Sun lights up the Moon, but stars make their own light.
wrong.2: The Moon makes no light of its own, so it cannot light the stars.

quiz.say: What do you call a pattern of stars in the sky?
quiz.show: ✨ A pattern of stars is a…
quiz.why: A constellation is a pattern of stars, like the Plough.

wrong.0: A planet, like Mars, goes around the Sun.
wrong.1: A galaxy is a huge group of billions of stars.
